BEEF
100% Grassfed, Grass Finished Beef

Greenacres produces 100% grassfed, grass finished beef in the Cincinnati area. Our cattle spend their entire lives roaming outdoors, eating fresh, living pasture during the growing season and high quality hay in the winter, a diet that suits their natural digestive processes making for healthy, happy cows. Our beef is always 100% grassfed and grass finished.

BEEF AVAILABLE YEAR ROUND

Check our product availability to see what we currently have in stock.

PRODUCT AVAILABILITY

The Greenacres Difference
100% grassfed and grass finished, never fed grain
Free to roam on pasture from birth to harvest day
No unnecessary antibiotics
Low stress calf weaning
Staff who love our animals
Butchers chosen with animal welfare in mind
Cattle rotated quickly through pasture
Without confinement, manure fertilizes grasses and improves the soil
Healthy soil sequesters carbon, holds rainwater
Higher Omega 3 and lower Omega 6 fatty acids (anti-inflammatory)
Fuller phytonutrient profile, including vitamins A and E (Learn More)
Lower overall fat content
A Responsible Protein Choice

How does 100% grassfed beef compare to plant-based “meat alternatives”? Ingredients used to produce these products (soy, peas, seed oils, rice, etc) are grown in huge, industrial agricultural operations that tend to specialize in and grow only one crop, a practice known as ‘monocropping’. Monocrop agriculture can harm the environment in many ways; compacting and degrading soils, using large quantities of pesticides and herbicides, polluting water, and harming biodiversity. Monocropped soils can be devoid of the lifeforms you’d find in healthy soils, like bacteria, invertebrates, insects, and fungi.

Raising cattle on pasture improves both the quality and quantity of soil biology, sequestering carbon and building biodiversity.

LEARN MORE

Our Genetics

For over 30 years, Greenacres has been developing a line of Angus genetics with excellent performance in grass based systems. Our farmers are constantly improving our herd; introducing genetic traits that make our cows finish better on grass, while our researchers study the farming practices that make products with better nutritional properties. This collaborative effort between farmers and scientists creates beef with excellent flavor, texture, and nutritional properties.

WHAT WE OFFER
PRODUCE

We offer a diverse variety of high-quality seasonal vegetables. Nourish yourself and your family with fresh produce that is organically grown, free of synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, and managed with growing methods like crop rotation, cover crops, integrated pest management, low/no-till, the rotational integration of livestock, and a living soil approach.

PASTURE RAISED EGGS
LEARN MORE

Our laying hens are free to forage and are never caged. They are rotated through our pastures in a mobile chicken coop with access to nesting boxes and water. Our laying hens receive a supplement of non-GMO feed without corn or soy. Brown eggs are collected and sold fresh daily.

100% GRASSFED GRASS-FINISHED BEEF
LEARN MORE

Our cattle spend their entire lives roaming outdoors, eating fresh, living pasture during the growing season and high-quality hay in the winter, a diet that suits their natural digestive processes making for healthy, happy cows. Our beef is always 100% grassfed and grass-finished

100% GRASSFED GRASS-FINISHED LAMB
LEARN MORE

Our sheep spend their entire lives on pasture, grazing fresh, living forage during the growing season and high-quality hay in the winter. This 100% grassfed, grass-finished diet aligns with their natural digestive systems, promoting healthy, low-stress animals. Our flocks are raised with sustainable rotational grazing practices.

WOODLAND RAISED PORK
LEARN MORE

Our hogs are raised outdoors in large wooded areas of our property, where they can seek out acorns, walnuts, roots, and other treats. In addition to the food they forage, we provide a high-quality, locally sourced hog feed to meet their nutritional needs. They also get regular deliveries of vegetable scraps from our gardens and the Farm Market.

PASTURE RAISED CHICKEN
LEARN MORE

Our chickens have a high quality of life. Living outdoors, they can express natural behaviors like scratching and pecking and eating their fill of bugs, grasses, and clover, to our mutual benefit.

PASTURE RAISED TURKEY
LEARN MORE

Our turkeys are free-range and graze on fresh pasture grasses. Greenacres turkeys are raised without artificial stimulants or antibiotics. Turkeys are a seasonal crop at Greenacres and are available fresh for the Thanksgiving holiday.

INDIAN HILL CSA PROGRAM

The Greenacres CSA is a flexible program that lets you shop at the Indian Hill Farm Market on your schedule. Your membership is loaded onto a store card that you can use to select the products you want, when you want them. There are no predetermined boxes, pickup times, or required volunteer hours, just use your card during market hours to enjoy our fresh produce, flowers, eggs, and meat products.

Participating in the CSA also directly supports Greenacres’ mission. Your membership helps provide hands-on learning opportunities for apprentices and students, supports agricultural research, and contributes to the care and stewardship of Greenacres’ land.

At this time, the CSA program is only available at the Indian Hill Farm Market. To join, stop by the market during open hours.

CSA FAQ
Do I need to use up my card by a certain date?

No, your CSA card does not expire and can be used at any time.

Are there membership levels?

Yes, you can load your CSA card with an amount that works best for you, and your card may be reloaded at any time.

Can I use my card for all Farm Market products?

Yes, your CSA card can be used on produce, flowers, eggs, and meat products. Discounts apply to produce, flowers, eggs, and ground beef.

Do I need to shop at a certain time?

No, your CSA card may be used whenever the Indian Hill Farm Market is open.

ABOUT US
EDUCATION, RESEARCH, CONSERVATION

Greenacres Foundation offers something for everyone. From exploring preserved forests and creeks, capturing beauty in music and artwork, to discovering secrets of farming and gardening. Come enjoy school field trips and summer camps as well as fresh produce from the farm store and special public events. Inspiration is contagious among Greenacres team who truly possess a passion for our Mission.

SIGN UP FOR OUR GREENACRES CINCINNATI NEWSLETTER

JOIN OUR MAILING LIST

OUR MISSION

Greenacres will always reflect the style and grace of Louis and Louise Nippert who operated Greenacres as a mid-twentieth century gentleman’s farm from 1948 to 2012.

To preserve for the public an area reflecting the traditional environment of Indian Hill and its historical significance by preserving Greenacres in its current state of woodland and farmland.

To preserve the integrity of all land owned and purchased by Greenacres Foundation in order to encourage conservation and appreciation of nature by providing the public, particularly children, opportunities to study plant and animal life in their natural settings.

To encourage appreciation of music and culture by providing facilities and an atmosphere that will encourage artists to display their talents for all age groups.

OUR VALUES
Giving

Louis and Louise Nippert were giving people. Greenacres is a gift from the Nippert’s and a gift to the community. Greenacres employees should always be giving of ourselves, to each other and the communities we serve.

Grace

Is the humble approach to life and the way our staff executes the Mission with the public. Each guest is made to feel special and the staff strives to make their visit memorable. Louis and Louise Nippert exhibited grace to any guest that entered their home; all visitors are special and are treated with the same respect, affection and grace. Every person is valued, welcomed, and treated with dignity and respect.

Green

Means always looking at the big picture, thinking holistically and considering all direct and indirect consequences of a decision on Greenacres, its guests and the environment (locally and globally). Everything is done to enhance and grow capacity and not to destroy it. Leave no trace.

Good Neighbor Policy

Is always being respectful of our neighbors and our guests and sharing our assets with the community. All guests and employees are treated with respect and equality. We are good teammates inside of Greenacres and anytime we are out in the community.

Generative

Is what we do. We build for the future in all ways. We build soil for agriculture productive capacity through our farming techniques, we build the woods by preserving them and protecting them from invasive species, we grow people through education of visitors to Greenacres and by on-going professional development of our staff. We do not inherit the earth from our grandparents, we borrow it from our grandchildren, and we must pay the loan back with interest. We must generate a better earth than we received.

OUR HISTORY

Louis and Louise Nippert purchased 47 acres of land known as Greenacres Farm from the Green family in 1949. Between 1949 and 1998, the Nipperts purchased several adjacent tracts of land and today the farm comprises nearly 600 acres. It was originally operated as a mid-twentieth century gentleman’s farm. In 1988, wanting to give back to the community, they started Greenacres Foundation with the intent to preserve the land for the education and enjoyment of future generations. Their mission lives on today, serving over 30,000 students a year, while expanding into new communities.

CAREERS
WORKING AT GREENACRES

We are a non-profit dedicated to conservation, generative agriculture, research, and providing immersive educational experiences focusing on nature, agriculture, music, and the arts. We are a certified Pony Club Riding Center and offer introductory horse-back riding lesson programs for children 8-18 years-old. Greenacres also hosts events including weddings, private events, and symphony concerts.

AVAILABLE POSITIONS

JOIN OUR TEAM

Greenacres Foundation offers exciting and engaging career paths for everyone!  We have a wide-variety of job opportunities throughout the organization. Whether you are looking for a mission-driven administrative or scientific role, a “hands-on” teaching position, or a profession working outdoors, Greenacres would love to get to know you!

We offer careers in the following Departments:

Administrative
Agriculture (Livestock & Garden)
Education (Environmental, Agricultural, Music, Art, and Water Quality) 
Equine 
Buildings & Grounds
Events
Research 

 

AVAILABLE POSITIONS

TOP WORKPLACE

We have been recognized as a Top Workplace for 2022! Greenacres is extremely proud of its employees, their contribution and dedication to the organization’s positive culture. We all thrive to create a team environment in which each member feels motivated, committed, and valued. We are constantly improving and growing. We offer professional training opportunities to all employees who have been with the company for more than six months.

EDUCATION INTERNSHIPS
INSPIRING THE NEXT GENERATION OF EDUCATORS

Greenacres offers a unique, year-long internship opportunity within our Education Department, with placements available in two dynamic divisions: Arts Education and Environmental Education. These full-time, paid positions include benefits and provide an immersive experience in informal education at a mission-driven nonprofit.

As an Education Intern, you’ll gain hands-on experience developing and delivering engaging, student-centered programs aligned with K–12 state and national learning standards. Interns will play a key role in guiding field trips, supporting summer camps, and creating meaningful, interactive learning experiences that inspire curiosity and connection to nature and the arts.

This internship is ideal for individuals seeking to build a strong foundation in education, environmental stewardship, and nonprofit work, while contributing to the Greenacres mission of fostering connections between people and the environment through education, research, and conservation.

INTERNSHIP INFORMATION

Applications Open: April
Internship Begins: August

APPLY NOW

EDUCATION DIVISIONS
ENVIRONMENT EDUCATION INTERNSHIP
LEARN MORE

The Greenacres Environment Education Internship is a one-year, full-time paid position designed for individuals passionate about outdoor education and environmental interpretation. Interns work alongside experienced educators to lead school field trips, after-school programs, and summer camps, using the natural landscapes of forests, ponds, streams, and fields as dynamic classrooms. Through hands-on training, mentorship, and immersive teaching experiences, interns develop practical skills in informal education while inspiring students to connect with the environment. This internship includes benefits, offers career preparation in the nonprofit sector, and provides opportunities to work across multiple Greenacres locations in Ohio and Indiana.

ARTS EDUCATION INTERNSHIP
LEARN MORE

The Greenacres Arts Education Internship is a one-year, full-time paid position offering hands-on experience in arts-based education through school field trips, after-school programs, and summer camps. Interns work closely with experienced educators to deliver engaging visual and performing arts programming in inspiring settings, including historic spaces, curated gardens, and natural woodlands. Designed for those pursuing careers in visual arts, performing arts, art history, or museum studies, this internship provides mentorship, training, and career development within a mission-driven nonprofit. With opportunities to teach, learn, and grow, interns will help students explore creativity and connect with the arts in meaningful ways.

GREENACRES ARTS EDUCATION
INTERNSHIP
INTERNING WITH THE ARTS EDUCATION TEAM

Greenacres Foundation offers a unique, one-year paid internship with our Arts Education Team, providing aspiring educators the opportunity to immerse themselves in creative, hands-on learning experiences. Interns actively contribute to field trip programs, after-school activities, and summer camps centered around the visual and performing arts.

Set within a historic home, curated gardens, and preserved woodlands, this internship offers a meaningful opportunity to engage with children through small-group instruction in an inspiring setting. If you’re passionate about arts education and interested in gaining practical experience in non-traditional, immersive teaching, we invite you to apply.

Each year, we select one intern. Applications open every April.

INTERNSHIP INFORMATION

Applications Open: April
Internship Begins: August

APPLY NOW

WHO CAN APPLY?

This internship is ideal for individuals interested in beginning or further developing a career in arts education. Applicants may have backgrounds in visual arts, performing arts, art history, or museum studies, and should demonstrate a genuine passion for creative learning and an interest in working with children. The Arts Education Team seeks individuals who are curious, collaborative, and self-motivated—those who are eager to grow as educators in a dynamic, hands-on learning environment.

We are committed to providing meaningful experiences for students through programs that integrate the visual and performing arts. If you are enthusiastic about teaching, enjoy working as part of a team, and are excited by the opportunity to make an impact through the arts, we encourage you to apply.

Applicants must be at least 18 years of age. While Greenacres does not provide housing, this is a paid internship and includes medical and dental benefits, along with paid holidays.

WHAT TO EXPECT

As an intern with the Greenacres Arts Education Team, you will become part of a dedicated group of professionals who are passionate about the arts, education, and the Greenacres mission. Throughout the one-year internship, you will receive mentorship and training in visual and performing arts content, informal education practices, program development, nature connection, and career readiness within a nonprofit setting.

The internship is based at our Indian Hill campus, with occasional travel required to support programming at our other education sites: Miami Township Clermont County (OH), Lewis Township (OH), and Oldenburg (IN). Flexibility is essential, as schedules and programming vary seasonally and according to educational needs.

You will be immersed in the daily operations of an innovative education team, gaining valuable experience in both planning and delivering engaging, arts-based lessons to a wide range of student groups.

TEACHING AT GREENACRES

As a member of the Arts Education Team, you will play an active role in delivering high-quality, hands-on programming in the visual and performing arts. This includes assisting with school field trips, after-school enrichment, and summer camp sessions. Interns work closely with students in small groups, helping to create meaningful, memorable experiences in our historic home, curated gardens, and surrounding natural spaces.

By the end of your internship, you will have developed a strong foundation in arts-based education and have the opportunity to share your experience and personal teaching philosophy in a presentation to the Greenacres staff. This capstone moment allows you to reflect on your growth and contributions while preparing for the next step in your professional journey.

GREENACRES ENVIRONMENT EDUCATION
INTERNSHIP
INTERNING WITH THE ENVIRONMENT EDUCATION TEAM

Greenacres offers a one-year, paid internship with our Environment Education Team, where you will gain hands-on experience delivering outdoor educational programming for school field trips and summer camps. Interns are immersed in dynamic, nature-based teaching, working with small groups of children in forests, streams, ponds, and fields. This is an exciting opportunity for individuals passionate about environmental education, outdoor learning, and nature interpretation to build practical skills in a non-traditional, experiential setting.

Each year, we welcome three new interns to join our team. Applications open in April.

INTERNSHIP INFORMATION

Applications Open: April
Internship Begins: August

APPLY NOW

WHO CAN APPLY?

This internship is ideal for individuals interested in beginning or enriching their careers in environmental education. Whether your background includes environmental studies, biology, education, outdoor leadership, or related fields, we encourage you to apply if you are enthusiastic about sharing the natural world with others. We are looking for passionate, inquisitive, and self-motivated individuals who are eager to grow as educators and contribute meaningfully to our mission.

Our team is committed to delivering inspiring and engaging educational experiences that foster curiosity, connection, and stewardship in students. If you enjoy collaborating with others, spending time outdoors, and helping young learners explore and understand nature, we invite you to apply.

Applicants must be at least 18 years of age. While Greenacres does not provide housing, this is a paid internship and includes medical and dental benefits, along with paid holidays.

WHAT TO EXPECT

As an Environment Education Intern, you will become part of a dedicated team of educators who care deeply about the natural world, collaborative teaching, and the mission of Greenacres. You will receive mentorship and training in environmental interpretation, natural history, experiential teaching strategies, and professional development within a nonprofit context.

Interns are based at one of our education sites in Indian Hill or Miami Township Clermont County (OH), with occasional travel to other Greenacres locations including Lewis Township (OH), and Oldenburg (IN). This position requires flexibility, adaptability, and a willingness to engage in diverse teaching environments across seasons and weather conditions.

TEACHING AT GREENACRES

Interns play an active role in planning and leading all aspects of Greenacres’ school field trips, after-school programs, and summer camps. You will help deliver high-quality, hands-on learning experiences in natural settings, sparking curiosity and fostering a sense of wonder in our students.

At the conclusion of the internship, each intern will have the opportunity to present their developed teaching philosophy and reflect on their experience with the full Greenacres staff, celebrating their growth as educators and their contributions to our community.
